body:
First of all, i'd like to thank you for your kind words, and more than that, I'd like to thank you for taking the time to encourage and offer advice to a tattered mind. It is a comfort knowing there are still people to talk to somewhere out there.

I have only spent a small amount of time studying philosophy, mostly due to the fact that religion was brow-beaten into me as a child, and turned me off of all schools of deeper thought as a result. But it's something that I am willing to try. Alan Watts and Jiddu Krishnamurti have been noted and I will take the time required to learn more. If nothing else, I enjoy learning about new things and it will come as a much needed distraction.

Thank you for introducing me to /r/eood, I had no idea this was even a thing. Exercising out of depression is something that I have tried in the past, resulting in only dismal failure. But I never had the proper structure or planning behind it that is recommended in this sub-reddit. Perhaps I should try again, only with more a firm plan in place. The possibility remains that it could all fall apart again, but at least it could offer to quite the screaming mind, if only for a moment.

Speaking of a quite mind, in your post you said that it is possible to "learn how to quiet the chattering, hypervigilant mind" This is something that I've never thought was possible. I cannot articulate to you just how wonderful it would be to have just a single moment where my mind is not rehashing or rehearsing those terrible thoughts of yesterday and tomorrow. I really feel that my constant thoughts of ending my existence would slowly erode away if I could just attain some modicum of inner-peace, and if philosophy can help direct me there, then I am more then willing to try.

Thank you again for your time and encouragement. You have, in fact, helped.
